preconditions.expression: T == int(stdin.split()[0]) and T >= 1 and T <= 100
preconditions.description: The first line of input is a single integer T (1 ≤ T ≤ 100) representing the number of test cases.

preconditions.expression: all(N == int(line) and N >= 2 and N <= 10000 and N % 2 == 0 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1::] if line.strip() and int(line.split()[0]) <= N)
preconditions.description: For each test case, the first line is an integer N (2 ≤ N ≤ 10000, even) representing the number of vertices in the tree.

preconditions.expression: all(len(edges) == N - 1 for edges in [stdin.splitlines()[i:i+N-1] for i in range(1, len(stdin.splitlines()), N)] if edges)
preconditions.description: Each test case has exactly N-1 edges, each edge is a pair of integers (u, v) where 1 ≤ u, v ≤ N.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(u) <= N and 1 <= int(v) <= N for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] if line.strip() and (u, v) := tuple(map(int, line.split())))
preconditions.description: Each edge (u, v) has vertices u and v within the range [1, N].

postconditions.expression: all(len(output_lines) == 3 * T for output_lines in [stdin.splitlines()[i:i+3] for i in range(0, len(stdin.splitlines()), 3)] if output_lines)
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output consists of exactly three lines: the minimum k, the set U, and the set V.

postconditions.expression: all(k == int(output_lines[0]) and k >= 0 for output_lines in [stdin.splitlines()[i:i+3] for i in range(0, len(stdin.splitlines()), 3)] if output_lines)
postconditions.description: The first line of each test case's output is an integer k, representing the minimum value of k such that H_k is good.

postconditions.expression: all(len(set(output_lines[1].split())) == N // 2 and len(set(output_lines[2].split())) == N // 2 for output_lines in [stdin.splitlines()[i:i+3] for i in range(0, len(stdin.splitlines()), 3)] if output_lines)
postconditions.description: The second and third lines of each test case's output contain exactly N/2 distinct integers each, representing the sets U and V.

postconditions.expression: all(set(output_lines[1].split()) | set(output_lines[2].split()) == set(str(i) for i in range(1, N + 1)) for output_lines in [stdin.splitlines()[i:i+3] for i in range(0, len(stdin.splitlines()), 3)] if output_lines and (N := int(stdin.splitlines()[i].strip())))
postconditions.description: The union of sets U and V contains all vertices from 1 to N exactly once.

postconditions.expression: all(any(all(int(v) in set(output_lines[1].split()) and int(u) in set(output_lines[2].split()) for u, v in edges) for edges in [get_edges_for_k(G, k) for k in range(int(output_lines[0]))] if edges) for output_lines in [stdin.splitlines()[i:i+3] for i in range(0, len(stdin.splitlines()), 3)] if output_lines and (G := get_tree_from_input(stdin.splitlines()[i+1:i+N])) and (k := int(output_lines[0])))
postconditions.description: For the computed k, the graph H_k is good, meaning there exists a partition (U, V) such that every edge in H_k connects U and V, and the bipartite graph is connected.
